role: Write a one-page guide that lets a busy teacher who has never used the platform, and may not be confident about AI, run the lesson in a 40-minute period with or without devices.
method: Read the whole lesson in classroom mode as a teacher with 45 students, one projector and no student devices.
Write the objectives in words a teacher could say aloud to the class.
Plan the 40 minutes block by block; include settling and wrap-up; the total must be 40 minutes or less.
For each likely misconception, write what students say and a good response the teacher can give, which must be accurate.
Give a no-device and no-projector alternative that still keeps every learner acting.
Write discussion prompts that have no single right answer.
Keep it to one page (about 600 words). Use plain words; explain any AI term in one line.

criteria.name: Runnable from the guide alone
criteria.description: A teacher who has never seen the platform could run the period from the guide: what to project, what to say, what students do, when to move on.

levels.4: Every segment says what to show, say and ask; transitions are clear; nothing needs the platform explained elsewhere.
levels.3: Runnable; one segment is vague about what students do.
levels.2: A teacher would need to explore the platform first.
levels.1: A description of the lesson, not a plan.

criteria.name: Realistic 40-minute timing
criteria.description: Timing fits a real Indian classroom period, including settling, voting by show of hands with 40+ students, and wrap-up.

levels.4: Realistic and fits with a buffer; says what to cut if time runs short.
levels.2: Overruns or ignores settling and wrap-up.

criteria.name: Accurate misconception responses
criteria.description: Likely misconceptions are listed with what students say and an accurate, simple response.

levels.4: The important misconceptions are covered and every response is accurate and sayable.
levels.2: One response is inaccurate or one key misconception is missing.

criteria.name: A real no-device path
criteria.description: Without devices or projector, every learner still acts (hands, paper, board).

levels.4: A complete alternative for every act, using board, paper and hands.

criteria.name: Builds teacher confidence
criteria.description: Plain, warm language; AI terms explained in one line; tells the teacher it is fine not to know and what to say then.

levels.4: A teacher unsure about AI would feel ready.
levels.3: Plain and supportive; one unexplained term.

ifYouDontKnow.description: What a teacher can say when a student asks something they cannot answer.
